problem:
Consider the following parametric equation of the parabola 

$$
x+2=4{t}^{2},\,y-1=8t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of this parabola is

$(y\,-$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{x+2}{4},\,t=\frac{y-1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{y-1}{8})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{x+2}{4}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{64} & =\frac{x+2}{4} \\ (y-1)^{2} & =64\cdot (\frac{x+2}{4}) \\ {(y-1)}^{2} & =16(x+2)\end{aligned}
$$
